- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes in history.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects by 5–10% in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts longer than observed price behavior suggests.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent declines.
- Model reacts too slowly to downward trends in history — fails to anticipate sharp drops in the next 5–7 days.
- When history includes a recent low, model often fails to recognize it as a bottom and continues to forecast upward.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 10 days — correction rules should prioritize adjusting early forecast values downward.
